candidates.source_summary: The battle for Hopwood Hall returns to the courtroom today with ownership of the historic manor house at stake.
candidates.source_title: Two days that will decide the future of Hopwood Hall - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The battle for Hopwood Hall returns to the courtroom today with ownership of the historic manor house at stake. Hopwood DePree and Rochdale Council begin a two-day trial in the High Court in Manchester later over Mr DePree’s bid to restore his ancestral home. Mr DePree is a descendant of the Hopwood family which build the manor house in the 1420s. The family owned the hall and surrounding land — which is now Hopwood Hall College — until 1922. The house was sold 20 years later. It was occupied by a variety of temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who ran it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. It had fallen into disrepair and was bought by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed property. The legal action initiated by Mr DePree was launched after he spent seven years working with the council to carry out vital repairs on the dilapidated site with a view to purchasing it. In November, 2024, the council ended its exclusivity agreement with Mr DePree, and said it would explore other options because no “commercially viable” business model had been presented. READ MORE: Four arrests and £1m drugs seizure in Rochdale Mr DePree’s case is that the council went back on his option to purchase Hopwood Hall upon planning permission being granted in 2022. His claim is that the agreement triggers have been satisfied and the council must proceed with the ownership transfer.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale Town Hall’s Martlet Kitchen wins Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice award
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The Martlet Kitchen at Rochdale Town Hall has won a Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award for 2026 following reviews from its customers. The award recognises businesses which consistently receive positive reviews, placing them among the top 10 per cent of listings on the review site. The restaurant opened in 2024 and is led by chef Darren Parkinson, who trained at Hopwood Hall College. He previously worked at Shibden Mill Inn in Halifax and the Fleece Inn in Ripponden. Its suppliers include Jacksons Farm in Milnrow, Defiance Distillery at Spotland Mill and Grandpa Greene’s in Oldham. Darren said: “This award is great news and we’re aiming for more accolades in the future. It’s about good old fashioned British grub, cooked to perfection, using top quality local ingredients, coupled with excellent service.” Restaurant manager Sarah Crabtree said the team regularly changes the menu while retaining dishes such as fish and chips. She said: “Everyone who works here takes huge pride in their job, so the experience for the customers is really consistent.” The Martlet Kitchen serves breakfast and lunch, with a grill club on Fridays and fine dining on Saturday evenings. It has also introduced private dining in the Mayor’s reception room at the Grade I listed town hall.

Greater Manchester Police said officers were called just before 6.15pm and a full search involving emergency services was undertaken. candidates.source_summary: The Atom Valley Northern Gateway Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) has appointed Chris Cheap as its managing director.
candidates.source_title: New managing director to lead Atom Valley’s Northern Gateway Regeneration - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The Atom Valley Northern Gateway Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) has appointed Chris Cheap as its managing director. Northern Gateway is a key part of the wider Atom Valley Mayoral Development Zone that stretches across Bury, Oldham, and Rochdale and plays a central role in supporting growth across advanced manufacturing, innovation, housing and infrastructure. The scheme has recently seen the completion of the base build of the 30,000 sq ft Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) within the 25-acre Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID) at Kingsway Park in Rochdale. Northern Gateway stands to be a significant driver of the reindustrialisation of Britain and a key contributor to the government’s Northern Growth Strategy. One of the key Northern Gateway projects will improve the highway connection between the site and M66 and M60 motorways needed to unlock the next phases of development and complement ongoing works to increase the capacity of the nearby Simister Island. The Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale join civic leaders at the newly completed Sustainable Materials and Manufacturing Centre Mr Cheap joins the MDC after almost 23 years at real estate advisor Avison Young where he held a number of leadership roles both regionally in the North West and nationally. Most recently, he led the UK transactional team overseeing capital markets, leasing and development across industrial, office and retail sectors.

candidates.source_title: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Seventeen people have been arrested as police tackle a “spider web of criminality” in Heywood and Rochdale. This morning, 250 officers carried out a series of raids as part of Operation Rivercrest which is targeting an organised crime group. The operation led to the execution of 20 warrants – mostly in Rochdale and Heywood – as well as in areas across Bury, Salford, Manchester, Merseyside and Yorkshire. Those arrested range in age from 19 to 49. Sixteen men have been arrested on suspicion of various offences, including drugs supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery. One woman, aged 21, was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of drugs. DS Hannah Taala, of Greater Manchester Police’s Rochdale Division, said officers focused on the crime group after violence in Heywood earlier in the year . She said: “There was a large disorder in April, where multiple people were involved in violence in the Heywood area. “It ended in some quiet serious injuries, assaults, a stab wound, using vehicles in that disorder, weapons, machetes. A cannabis farm was discovered during the raids. Image: GMP

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Grimsby Town ended their four-game losing streak in the league with a frantic 2-2 draw away at Rochdale on Tuesday evening. It could have easily been better for the Mariners, though, who led late on following a second-half comeback with goals from captain Kieran Green and Jamie Walker after Dajaune Brown’s 38th-minute opener for the hosts. Rochdale’s 41-year-old striker Ian Henderson had the final say off the bench as he headed in an 88th-minute equaliser to ensure a share of the points, as Town once again rued missed opportunities. David Artell made a shape change for this game, with his squad needing some inspiration and also lacking in defensive bodies. Town moved to a back three shape with Joe Foulkes coming in for his full league debut and Andy Cook returning to the starting line-up in place of the injured Edon Pruti and Doug Tharme. Cook and Iwan Morgan were a central tandem up top, with Charles Vernam and Justin Amaluzor asked to do more defensively as wing-backs. Foulkes slotted in as the third centre-back alongside Harvey Rodgers and Maldini Kacurri. The home side made the brighter start, Glenn Middleton’s shot being cleared off the line by Foulkes, with the latter proving his worth as a defender early into his first league start. Morgan had a 20-yard shot blocked early, and Charles Vernam wanted a penalty in the sixth minute as he went down in the box under duress from Harvey Gilmour, but instead, he received a yellow card for simulation. candidates.source_title: Here's what a major housing scheme in Rochdale could look like according to new plans
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Seven blocks on Rochdale’s Lower Falinge estate are set to be demolished to make way for 270 new homes . Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have officially submitted plans to the council to bulldoze Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zedburgh and Vaynor. Once they are demolished RBH would start work on building a mixture of homes and flats, all available for social rent. The majority of the 270 homes would go on the land due to be bulldozed – next to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road to the west. There are plots east of the giant estate, near to Redcross Street, that would also be built on under the proposals. RBH bought up the land to the east in recent years, just next to St Mary’s Gate. The proposals, if approved by Rochdale council, also intend to create new landscaping, public open spaces, safer streets, and new walking routes into the town centre. RBH says they have to demolish the seven remaining blocks because they are at the end of their life and no longer provide safe, warm homes. Six of the blocks have been empty for years. Only Zedburgh remains occupied by Andy Roche and his partner.

Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have officially submitted plans to the council to bulldoze Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zedburgh and Vaynor. Once they are demolished RBH would start work on building a mixture of homes and flats, all available for social rent. The majority of the 270 homes would go on the land due to be bulldozed – next to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road to the west. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter There are plots east of the giant estate, near to Redcross Street, that would also be built on under the proposals. RBH bought up the land to the east in recent years, just next to St Mary’s Gate. The proposals, if approved by Rochdale council , also intend to create new landscaping, public open spaces, safer streets, and new walking routes into the town centre. RBH says they have to demolish the seven remaining blocks because they are at the end of their life and no longer provide safe, warm homes. Six of the blocks have been empty for years. Only Zedburgh remains occupied by Andy Roche and his partner . When RBH’s initial vision was revealed two months ago, Andy said: “Obviously it’s extremely distressing for me because it involves being forced out of my home. I am not happy about RBH’s proposals, but I’m not sure how to put it into words. “I’m still processing it. candidates.source_summary: Veteran striker Ian Henderson came off the bench to rescue a point for Rochdale with an 88th-minute leveller as they drew 2-2 with Grimsby.
candidates.source_title: Rochdale 2-2 Grimsby - Sky Sports
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Veteran striker Ian Henderson came off the bench to rescue a point for Rochdale with an 88th-minute leveller as they drew 2-2 with Grimsby.

The 41-year-old converted Charlie Tasker's cross from close range at the end of a high-octane clash at the Crown Oil Arena.

The home side made the brighter start, Glenn Middleton's shot being cleared off the line by Joe Foulkes.

Grimsby's best effort of the half came from Charles Vernam, a fierce shot saved by Dale goalkeeper Sam Waller.

Rochdale took the lead in the 38th minute when Middleton got in behind the Mariners' backline and fired an inviting cross to the back post where Dajaune Brown slid in and side-footed home.

Grimsby levelled in the 57th minute, Harvey Rodgers' delivery to the back post picking out Andy Cook and though Waller saved his header, Kieran Green was there to nod home.

The visitors took the lead in the 72nd minute when Jamie Walker collected a partially-cleared corner and slammed a low shot through a crowded penalty, but Henderson denied the Mariners victory with a poacher's finish.

candidates.source_summary: Ian Watson lauds ‘amazing’ Ian Henderson after late Rochdale leveller Clacton and Frinton Gazette
candidates.source_title: Ian Watson lauds ‘amazing’ Ian Henderson after late Rochdale leveller - Clacton and Frinton Gazette
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Manager Ian Watson hailed ‘amazing’ Ian Henderson after the 41-year-old striker rescued a point for Rochdale in a 2-2 draw against Grimsby at the Crown Oil Arena. Henderson came off the bench in the 81st minute with Dale trailing 2-1 and was in the right place to turn home Charlie Tasker’s delivery seven minutes later to secure a share of the spoils. Watson said: “It was a really hard game. I’d said to the boys beforehand that we were up against a really good side with a really good manager in David Artell. “They have a really aggressive way of playing off the ball and it wasn’t just from restarts, it was man v man for most of the game. In those moments we have to be good with the ball and I thought we could have been a bit braver but it is really hard against such an aggressive opponent. “It was a game that ebbed and flowed, we had the momentum, then they had it. We spoke to the lads at half-time about what we needed to improve on but we weren’t able to carry any momentum from that first half into the second and they came out a bit better than us. “But even when we conceded the second goal I felt there was something in it for us and I don’t even have any words for Ian Henderson, he’s an amazing guy and an amazing footballer.” Dale took the lead in the 38th minute when Glenn Middleton crossed for Dajaune Brown to slide home the opener. But the Mariners, on the back of a four-game losing streak, turned the game on its head with Kieran Green levelling in the 57th minute and Jamie Walker firing them ahead 15 minutes later.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Manager Ian Watson hailed ‘amazing’ Ian Henderson after the 41-year-old striker rescued a point for Rochdale in a 2-2 draw against Grimsby at the Crown Oil Arena. Henderson came off the bench in the 81st minute with Dale trailing 2-1 and was in the right place to turn home Charlie Tasker’s delivery seven minutes later to secure a share of the spoils. Watson said: “It was a really hard game. I’d said to the boys beforehand that we were up against a really good side with a really good manager in David Artell. “They have a really aggressive way of playing off the ball and it wasn’t just from restarts, it was man v man for most of the game. In those moments we have to be good with the ball and I thought we could have been a bit braver but it is really hard against such an aggressive opponent. “It was a game that ebbed and flowed, we had the momentum, then they had it. We spoke to the lads at half-time about what we needed to improve on but we weren’t able to carry any momentum from that first half into the second and they came out a bit better than us. “But even when we conceded the second goal I felt there was something in it for us and I don’t even have any words for Ian Henderson, he’s an amazing guy and an amazing footballer.” Dale took the lead in the 38th minute when Glenn Middleton crossed for Dajaune Brown to slide home the opener. But the Mariners, on the back of a four-game losing streak, turned the game on its head with Kieran Green levelling in the 57th minute and Jamie Walker firing them ahead 15 minutes later.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Veteran striker Ian Henderson came off the bench to rescue a point for Rochdale with an 88th-minute leveller as they drew 2-2 with Grimsby. The 41-year-old converted Charlie Tasker’s cross from close range at the end of a high-octane clash at the Crown Oil Arena. The home side made the brighter start, Glenn Middleton’s shot being cleared off the line by Joe Foulkes. Grimsby’s best effort of the half came from Charles Vernam, a fierce shot saved by Dale goalkeeper Sam Waller. Rochdale took the lead in the 38th minute when Middleton got in behind the Mariners’ backline and fired an inviting cross to the back post where Dajaune Brown slid in and side-footed home. Grimsby levelled in the 57th minute, Harvey Rodgers’ delivery to the back post picking out Andy Cook and though Waller saved his header, Kieran Green was there to nod home. The visitors took the lead in the 72nd minute when Jamie Walker collected a partially-cleared corner and slammed a low shot through a crowded penalty, but Henderson denied the Mariners victory with a poacher’s finish.

The produce weighed more than 60,000kg and was distributed through the programme, which Tesco developed in partnership with the British Nutrition Foundation. Apples were the most popular choice among participating Greater Manchester schools, accounting for around 221,000 portions. Bananas followed with around 103,000 portions, ahead of satsumas and clementines with around 88,000. Schools in Rochdale received a share of the regional total, although a separate figure for the borough was not provided. Tesco said almost 20 million portions had been eaten through the programme across the UK during its first two years, reaching up to 186,000 pupils. Now in its third year, the scheme has expanded to support more than 1,000 schools. According to the programme’s impact report, 98% of teachers surveyed said it encouraged pupils to eat a wider variety of fruit, while 94% reported improved behaviour. More than 1,500 tonnes of produce have been provided since the programme began, with pupils trying 103 types of fruit and vegetables.

candidates.source_summary: Plans for a direct rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again.
candidates.source_title: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to improve the rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again. Today, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays . Among those backing calls for the extra services was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who called Lumo’s bid to restore six daily direct services between Rochdale and the capital a “game-changing opportunity” for the borough and the wider North West. But the ORR rejected the plans after its assessment found adding more trains to the West Coast Main Line — which also included services to Blackpool and Wrexham — would likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers. It said its assessment following detailed and extensive analysis is that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the West Coast Main Line has not materially changed since it rejected a similar application by Lumo last year. An external review commissioned by ORR also supported this conclusion. READ MORE: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ The ORR said gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers.

The proposals also include demolishing seven remaining blocks. The application covers two sites, on land near Redcross Street and next to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road. RBH said the proposed mix of apartments and family homes would increase the number of bed spaces in the community by more than 300. The housing provider said the seven blocks proposed for demolition were at the end of their life and would no longer be able to provide safe, warm homes. The plans also include landscaping, public open spaces, safer streets and new walking routes. RBH said the homes would be designed to meet the Future Homes Standard, with measures intended to reduce energy use and heating costs. They would also be accessible and adaptable to residents’ changing needs. Hannah Fleming, RBH director of regeneration and asset improvement, said residents, businesses, community groups and local stakeholders had been consulted before the application was submitted. candidates.source_summary: A court has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to pass ownership of Hopwood Hall to one of its descendants.
candidates.source_title: Court rules in ownership row over Hopwood Hall - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A court has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to pass ownership of Hopwood Hall to one of its descendants. Today marked the end of a two-day trial in the High Court in Manchester after Hopwood DePree took legal action against the council which ended an exclusivity agreement to sell the historic Grade II-listed hall to him. Following the decision, Mr DePree said: “This is of course incredibly disappointing and a huge blow to our community, our supporters around the world, as well as the UK’s charitable heritage rescue groups in general. “However, please know that my team and I are already determining our legal options and next steps. “We will be watching closely to keep an eye on Rochdale Borough Council’s efforts to save Hopwood Hall for the community, and restore it to its former glory.” Mr DePree is a descendant of the Hopwood family which build the manor house in the 1420s. The family owned the hall and surrounding land — which is now Hopwood Hall College — until 1922. The house was sold 20 years later. It was occupied by a variety of temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who ran it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. It had fallen into disrepair and was bought by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed property. READ MORE:Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026 Finalists Announced

candidates.source_title: Inspector rules on garden fence rejected by council - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Three emerging Rochdale artists will receive free studio space, materials funding and support to develop work for a joint exhibition. Richard Street Studios and Breaking Barriers have named Alisha K., Madison Marcantonatos and Georgia Scholes as recipients of support funded by The Haworth Trust. Each artist will receive ten free days at Richard Street Studios, with the studio time valued at an estimated £1,200 per artist. The package also includes a materials budget and technical and marketing support. The scheme aims to help artists establish their practice in Rochdale. Parvez Qadir, artistic director at Breaking Barriers, said, “Rochdale has no shortage of creative talent. What it has lacked is the financial support for artists to take that talent seriously at the start of their careers.” Alisha K., who works with oil paint and pastel, said this would be her first opportunity to work in a professional studio alongside other artists. She said, “By the end, I hope to have pushed my practice further and created a body of work that reflects what I can do.” Multidisciplinary artist Madison Marcantonatos plans to explore nostalgia and her own experiences.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A 15-year-old girl is facing charges after Regina police seized a BB handgun while investigating a weapons call. Police were called to the 5200 block on Rochdale Boulevard a 6 p.m. on Oct. 17, after receiving a report that three females were in possession of what appeared to be a firearm. According to a news release, officers arrived within minutes and located two girls matching the suspect description in the 4400 block of Rochdale Boulevard. During a search, police found a BB handgun in the waistband of one of the girls. Police later determined the second girl was in possession of the BB handgun during the incident, according to RPS. candidates.source_title: ‘Nobody should face it alone — Sleep Out isn’t about pretending to be homeless’ - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Fundraisers spent a night outdoors to raise awareness and vital funds for people experiencing homelessness in the community. Supporters from across the borough came together at Rochdale’s Crown Oil Arena for the second Petrus Communities and RAFC Community Trust annual Sleep Out. Money raised will again go towards helping people through Changing Lives — a football initiative designed to support people experiencing homelessness or living in supported accommodation. The programme aims to improve participants’ mental health, physical well-being, and social inclusion through free, inclusive football sessions. It also provides personal development opportunities, including pathways into volunteering, education, and employment. Louise Scriven, Fundraising and Partnerships Coordinator at Petrus, said: “The Sleep Out isn’t about pretending to experience homelessness. It’s about standing alongside those who facing housing insecurities and homelessness, and to offer participants a small insight into some of the challenges faced by people who do not have a safe place to call home, while raising funds to support the work Petrus delivers every day across Rochdale, Oldham, and Burnley. “Last year’s event made a real difference and is helping people rebuild confidence, make new friendships, develop new skills and become active members of their community. The funds from last year partly helped set up the Changing Lives partnership program with Rochdale AFC Community Trust, who hosted the Sleep Out. “Every donation made helps us continue providing accommodation, support, advice and opportunities for people experiencing homelessness and disadvantage locally.
